objections.claim: Candidate artifact sha256:76ec1b2688a28a258f51605aa695914fe3fe62b829f8321b3c1b6776e4528f permits an external executable’s identity to be established by an absolute path plus a pinned version instead of requiring cryptographic byte identity. A replacement at the same path can report the expected version and then open a listener; the stated PATH-wrapper fixture does not discriminate this case. Even a separately recorded digest is insufficient unless it is verified and bound to the executable at each invocation without a path replacement race. This violates the content-address-not-mutable-label invariant and leaves the no-listener claim unsound. Require digest/equivalent authenticated package identity with mutation-point execution binding, plus a regression where a same-path binary reports the pinned version but attempts to listen and is refused before execution.

Candidate artifact sha256:76ec1b2688a28a258f51605aa695914fe3fe62b829f8321b3c1b6776e4528f constrains only the top-level Git binary, argv, and environment, not executables Git can launch. Git’s documented security contract states that configuration and hooks in an untrusted .git directory may run arbitrary shell commands; core.fsmonitor specifically lets `git status` execute an external hook. Checkout-mode verification operates on the connected repository, so repository-local configuration survives merely clearing global/system environment and rejecting top-level `-c` arguments. An allowlisted `git status --porcelain` can therefore launch an unallowlisted helper that opens a listener while every stated argv/identity regression remains green. Require deterministic suppression or validation of repository-local execution-bearing configuration and hooks plus confinement/recursive binding of all Git descendants, with a malicious core.fsmonitor/helper regression proving no descendant executes or listener opens.
